answer: Yes, you can withdraw after the census date, but there are academic and financial penalties. Withdrawing late means no fee refund, and the unit is recorded as WDN or as a WN fail grade, depending on the code.

points.text: After the census date you will be liable for your fees, because no refund is available.
points.quote: Financial: no refund available (you’ll be liable for your fees)
points.title: Add or withdraw from units

points.text: A late withdrawal recorded as WD-LATE shows as WDN on your transcript and is not counted in WAM or GPA, while WD-FAIL shows as a WN fail grade that counts as zero.
points.quote: recorded on transcript as a 'WN' fail grade (grade of zero included in calculating WAM and GPA)
points.title: Add or withdraw from units

points.text: If special circumstances beyond your control caused you to withdraw or fail after the census date, you may apply for a fee reversal and have a fail grade converted to WDN, within 12 months of the withdrawal date.
points.quote: your fail grade converted to a WDN grade
points.title: Fee reversal and Withdrawn grade (special circumstances)
points.section: Fee reversal and Withdrawn grade (special circumstances)

points.text: You cannot withdraw from units after the last day to withdraw shown in the teaching weeks end date.
points.quote: Last day to withdraw from units. After this date, you cannot withdraw from units.
points.title: Add or withdraw from units
